column1: # The mutation corpus: each row corrupts one documented line of a pinned
# corpus repository and names the verdict kibble must reach on the damage.
# The healthy line's verdict is already pinned by repos.tsv, so together the
# two files hold the property the tool exists for: correct documentation
# comes back green and one edit of rot flips it.
# The expected count is the mutated tree's own count, earned by a real run,
# never baseline plus one: a dead install skips the sessions behind it, so a
# mutation can lower other counts while it raises its own. The proof column
# pins identity: some finding with that status must name the mutated token,
# so a coincidental count cannot pass for a catch. Columns are tab-separated:
# name, clone URL, pinned commit, file, find, replace, STATUS=count, proof.
ripgrep
# The rich-cli row expected GAP=2 until 2026-09-08. kibble has always answered
# a brew name that resolves nowhere with FAIL, which is what docs/DESIGN.md
# says it should and what the unit suite already asserted, so the row was
# wrong rather than the engine. It went unnoticed because the job compared a
# status nothing emits and every row read as failing. Verified the same way
# the repos.tsv counts were: kibble built before and after the change that
# uncovered it answers FAIL=1 naming richhh either way.
rich-cli
# The healthy rows pinned no GAP after 2026-10-26, so this row pins one. A
# documented file that no step creates is reported as the document's gap. The
# section entered its own directory and sits under no block the plan left out,
# so the verdict rests on the file check alone. Earned by a real run: GAP=1
# with the detail naming READMEE.md, counts 2,0,1, exit 0.
ripgrep
